verdict.rationale: The evidence pack shows the B200 is an NVIDIA Tensor Core GPU shipped with NVIDIA's software stack (NVIDIA Container Toolkit, nvidia-smi). It also shows the CUDA platform is documented for building GPU-accelerated data-center applications, with architecture-specific tuning. However, no cited CUDA documentation explicitly names the B200 as a supported compile or runtime target. Support is therefore implied rather than explicitly listed. Missing for 10: an explicit CUDA toolkit or compute-capability support entry naming B200/Blackwell, driver/toolkit version requirements, and hands-on corroboration of CUDA workloads running on B200.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ship GPU-compute workloads on the vendor's toolchain — CUDA or ROCm/HIP documentation lists this part as a supported target

citations.quote: The system is built on eight NVIDIA B200 Tensor Core GPUs.
It enables engineers to build, optimize, debug, and deploy high-performance GPU-accelerated applications across data center, workstation, cloud, and embedded environments.
covering installation, programming models, architecture-specific tuning, runtime and driver APIs, math and utility libraries, compiler and PTX interfaces, debugging and profiling tools
